content.thinking: For वी (to go, parasmaipada), I'm working through lot forms: वेतु, वीतात्, वीताम्, वियन्तु for others; वीहि, वीतम्, वीत for madhyama; and for uttama, since आट् is pit, guna applies giving वयानि, वयाव, वयाम for the bahuvacana form.

For लिह् (adadi, ubhayapada, svarita), first person dual present: both parasmaipada लिह्वः and atmanepada लिह्वहे are valid, but लिह्वः is the standard answer. Since व isn't a jhal sound, ढोढः doesn't apply, so there's no further modification—लिह्वः stands as is.
पूञ् being ubhayapadi, for parasmaipada lot uttama bahuvacana I get श्ना + आम → पुना + आम → पुनाम, applying the shortening rule for प्वादि roots.

I'm tracing the root tig in svadi class, parasmaipada, with the nu-affix forming tignu-. For the lot uttama dual, I'm working through the guna and augment to derive tignavāva, checking the applicable lopa rule for the consonant preceding nu.
I'm working through the 9th class root viṣ, parasmaipada, deriving the lot uttama dual form viṣṇāva — checking how śnā combines with the ṇatva rule and the āṭ augment before the vowel ending.

This root ग्रह् takes svarita accent and is ubhayapadi, so I need first person plural present for both pada forms — परस्मैपदे गृह्णीमः and आत्मनेपदे गृह्णीमहे — and I'll go with गृह्णीमः as the answer.

I'm checking the root tu in the adādi class, confirming it's parasmaipada with anudātta accent, and looking into whether iṭ augment rules like 7.3.95 apply to its sārvadhātuka forms.

For Lot uttama dual, since āṭ augment makes the suffix pit, guṇa applies to tu giving tavāva — similar to how yu forms yavāni/yavāva/yavāma, since the vowel-initial suffix blocks the utovṛddhi rule.
Since this root is ubhayapadi and ñit, I can form both parasmaipada and atmanepada in lot uttama dual. For parasmaipada, applying guṇa to the root gives cinavāva (चिनवाव).
For aś (class 9, to eat), lan first person dual uttama needs vas→va with the ī-insertion rule before weak endings, plus the augment ā giving āśnīva.

I'm recalling that शॄ (to injure) belongs to kryādi gaṇa 9, with its present tense शृणाति governed by the pvādi rule shortening the vowel — noting it's part of that special pvādi group of roots like पूञ्, लूञ्, स्तॄञ्, कॄञ्, वृञ् and others sharing this vowel treatment.
For रु (to sound), the uttama purusha lot form is रवाम — the आम ending starts with a vowel so ईट् augment doesn't apply, and guna of रु gives रव्, yielding रवाम.

I'm working through श्रथ् (class 9 kryādi root), applying nasal deletion before the क्ङित् affix to get श्रथ्नाति, then figuring out the lot uttama puruṣa bahuvacana form with the आट् augment added to मस्.

Since श्ना is apit sārvadhātuka (treated like ṅit), the nasal still drops giving श्रथ्ना, and adding आम् yields श्रथ्नाम — matching known forms like ग्रथ्नाति.

For jahāti (to abandon) in laṅ, first person dual: applying rule 6.4.116 jahāteśca, the hal-ādi kṅit sārvadhātuka ending gets इ optionally, which becomes ई by 6.4.113 before hal. With lopo yi from 6.4.118, I get अजहीव or अजहिव, settling on अजहीव.
The root कृञ् is class 5 ubhayapadi, meaning हिंसा. For vidhiliṅ uttama bahu, parasmaipada gives कृणुयाम, formed on the analogy of सुनुयाम since कृ + श्नु becomes कृणु.

I'm working through प्री in vidhiliṅ uttama dvivacana — since it's a k
The root ci is ubhayapadi, so I can form either parasmaipada or atmanepada for first person dual vidhilin. Parasmaipada gives cinuyāva (alongside cinuyām, cinuyāma), so that's the form to give.

I'm working out the optative form of the root san (Tanadi class 8), comparing it to tan to figure out whether the u-vowel drops before the y, considering the optional lopa rule for u before m/v.

Since the root is ubhayapadi, both the parasmaipada सनुयाम and atmanepada सन्वीमहि forms are grammatically valid, but I'll settle on सनुयाम.

For तुभ् (kryadi, class 9, parasmaipada, meaning hiṃsā), the loṭ uttama puruṣa bahuvacana would take the āṭ augment before mas, giving तुभ्नाम, analogous to क्रीणाम — no ṇatva applies since there's no र् or ष् involved.

The root ष्टिघ् (stigh, meaning āskandana) belongs to Svādi gaṇa and is ātmanepadī due to the anudātta marking, giving stighnute as the base form. For lot uttama dual ātmanepada, I need to work out stighnavāvahai.

Since āṭ is added and the ending is pit, the u of the nu-pratyaya undergoes guṇa to become nau, giving stighnavāvahai. The optional lopa of u before m/v doesn't apply here since the u is preceded by a conjunct (gh+n) and āvahai begins with ā rather than directly with v, so the final form stands as स्तिघ्नवावहै.

I'm checking the root षणु (to give), from the tanadi group, and recalling that these roots are typically ubhayapadi, so the accent mThe root षणु (to give) is a tanadi class, ubhayapadi verb. For loṭ uttama parasmaipada bahuvacana, I need सन् + उ with आट् augment giving आम ending, and since it's pit, guna applies to उ turning it to अव — giving सनवाम, parallel to तनोति → तनवाम.
For āp with lot uttama bahuvacana, the u before -āma triggers guṇa since the āṭ augment is pit not ṅit, giving āpno + āma → āpnavāma.

I'm working through the root stu (ष्टुञ्, adadi, ubhayapada) in lan, checking the uttama dvivacana parasmaipada forms astuva/astuvīva, and verifying the relevant sutras governing the optional iṭ augment for this sārvadhātuka ending.

I'm working through ग्रन्थ् as a class 9 parasmaipada root, applying the श्ना nasal infix and checking the अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति rule to drop the nasal, giving ग्रथ्नाति; then I'm forming the lot uttama forms ग्रथ्नानि, ग्रथ्नाव, ग्रथ्नाम while sorting out whether आट् counts as पित् for these endings.

Since श्ना is sārvadhātuka and अपित्, it qualifies as ङित् via सार्वधातुकमपित्, so nasal elision applies regardless of the आट्'s पित्-status — matching बध्नानि, बध्नाव, बध्नाम for बन्ध्. Applying ई हल्यघोः for ग्रथ्नीमः in लट्, and for लोट् उत्तम with आट् added to म, the आ is dropped via श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः, yielding ग्रथ्न् + आम = ग्रथ्नाम as the final answer.

I'm working through the root तिग् (svādi class, parasmaipada) and its present tense forms, checking whether rule 6.4.107 for optional u-elision applies to तिग्नु, since the u here follows n rather than a conjunct cluster.

Since the u is preceded by the conjunct ग्न, which counts as saṃyogapūrva, the optional lopa doesn't apply—similar to आप्नुवः and शक्नुवः. There's also no vowel-initial suffix following to trigger yaṇ/uvaṅ changes, since वस् begins with v. So the correct first dual form is तिग्नुवः.

I'm checking the root पृ in the juhotyadi class — it's typically पॄ पालनपूरणयोः with long ॠ, but here it's marked short and anudatta (aniT), so I'm reconciling which Dhatupatha reading applies.

For reduplication, अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च gives इ in the abhyasa yielding पिपृ, and since this is apit sarvadhatuka with no guna, the लन् उत्तम बहुवचन form comes out as अपिपृम (distinct from अपिपूर्म for the long-vowel root).

I'm checking jñā's class and padī status - it's parasmaipada since it's aniṭ without any ṅit marker, so for laṅ uttama dvivacana in kartari prayoga, the form should be ajānīva.

For the construction, nā gets replaced by ī before a hal-ādi apit sārvadhātuka affix per the ī halyaghoḥ rule, giving ajānīva as the dual form (alongside ajānām and ajānīma for the other persons).

I'm working through the optative first plural of रु (adadi class, meaning "to cry/sound") — getting रुयाम since the root ends in u and यासुट् doesn't trigger guna before a consonant. I'm also checking whether 7.3.95's optional iṭ augment for certain hal-final roots could apply here.

Considering the alternative, if इट् is inserted before सार्वधातुक, it would give रुवीयाम (ru + īṭ + yām with uvaṅ before ī), so both रुयाम and रुवीयाम should be valid — I'll go with रुयाम as the answer.

I'm tracing the root खव् in the kryādi gaṇa, meaning भूतप्रादुर्भावे ("coming into being"), noting the variant reading खच and how the v changes to ū by the rule च्छ्वोः शूडनुनासिके च, giving forms like खौनाति.

I then work through the conjugation for uttama puruṣa bahuvacana: खौनानि for mip, and for mas, the āṭ augment makes it pit, combining śnā with āma to give खौनाम.
Since krī is ubhayapadi, I can form the lot uttama dual in either parasmaipada or atmanepada; going with parasmaipada gives क्रीणाव.
For वृङ् (to choose), a kryādi class ātmanepada root, the lot uttama dvivacana form is वृणावहै, formed by adding आवहै to the stem वृणा, analogous to क्रीणावहै.

I'm trying to recall the exact Dhatupatha entry for the kryadi root "khav" meaning "to appear/manifest" and its precise conjugated form.

Checking the relevant sutra on v → ūṭh substitution before anunāsika-initial affixes, which gives the form "khaunāti" via vṛddhi, and then working out the optative form "khaunīyāma" using the kryadi nā→nī rule before haladi ṅit sārvadhātuka affixes.
